name: Malapert Massif
summary: A mountain thought to be a remnant of the South Pole-Aitken basin rim. It is one of NASA's nine candidate landing regions for Artemis III (NASA release 24-136, October 2024).

tempMean.source: LRO Diviner Polar Resource Product, PDS LRO-L-DLRE-5-PRP-V2.0 (Paige et al. 2010, Science 330:479): mean of annual average temperature over a 55.6 km window (validation/build/moon_temperature.py)
tempMean.note: Annual average at 2 cm depth from the Diviner team's thermal model, averaged over the 55.6 km window. Sunlit ridges and shadowed floors inside the window differ by more than 100 K.

tempRange.note: No value. A lunar day lasts 29.53 Earth days and at the pole the Sun circles the horizon, so a daily max-minus-min swing like Earth's has no counterpart here, and no published site value was found.

precip.source: NASA NSSDC Moon Fact Sheet: surface pressure 3 x 10^-15 bar, so no rain or snow can form

ndvi.source: NASA Earth Observatory, Measuring Vegetation (NDVI and EVI): NDVI of 0.1 and below is barren rock, sand or snow
ndvi.note: Reference value for bare ground on Earth's NDVI scale. Not measured on the Moon.

slope.source: LRO LOLA polar gridded DEM LDEM_80S_80M (NASA PDS), measured with pipeline/terrain_metrics.py over a 55.6 km window (validation/target_terrain.py)

roughness.source: LRO LOLA polar gridded DEM LDEM_80S_80M (NASA PDS), measured with pipeline/terrain_metrics.py over a 55.6 km window (validation/target_terrain.py)

lithology.source: Flahaut et al. 2020, Planetary and Space Science 180:104750 (highland crust covered in South Pole-Aitken ejecta); LROC featured image 1294
lithology.note: GLiM class 4, Basic plutonic rocks. Chosen by SBATS: lunar highland crust is anorthosite, a plutonic rock of calcium-rich feldspar. No direct rock measurement at this site was found: the massif is described as highland crust under basin ejecta.

cannotCopy: Gravity: 1.62 m/s2 at the lunar surface against 9.80 m/s2 on Earth, about one sixth (NASA NSSDC Moon Fact Sheet).
Vacuum: the surface pressure at night is about 3 x 10^-15 bar, effectively no atmosphere (NASA NSSDC Moon Fact Sheet).

Radiation: the Chang'e 4 lander measured an average dose equivalent of 1,369 microsieverts per day on the lunar surface, with no atmosphere or magnetic field to shield it (Zhang et al. 2020, Science Advances).

Light: the Moon's spin axis is tilted by only 1.54 degrees (NASA Photojournal PIA13720), so at the pole the Sun stays at the horizon all year, ridges can be lit for months and crater floors never are. Earth's polar day and night do not behave this way.
Day length: one lunar day lasts 29.53 Earth days (NASA NSSDC Moon Fact Sheet), so warm and cold periods last weeks, not hours.

name: Haworth

name: Shackleton rim
summary: The rim of the 21 km crater that sits almost exactly on the south pole. A point near the rim is in sunlight continuously for 240 days of the year (Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus), next to a floor in permanent shadow. 'Peak near Shackleton' and 'Connecting Ridge' were on NASA's 2022 list of Artemis III candidate regions (release 22-089) but not on the 2024 list.

name: Jezero crater
summary: A 45 km crater that held a lake and a river delta about 3.5 billion years ago. NASA's Perseverance rover landed here on 18 February 2021 to study those deposits and collect samples.

tempMean.source: Mars Climate Database v6.2 (LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES), climatology scenario, air temperature 2 m above the surface (validation/build/mars_temperature.py)
tempMean.note: Climate model value. The Perseverance MEDA team reports a mean air temperature of around -55 C (UPV/EHU release on Rodriguez-Manfredi et al. 2023), which agrees.

tempRange.source: Mars Climate Database v6.2 (LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES), climatology scenario, air temperature 2 m above the surface (validation/build/mars_temperature.py)
tempRange.note: Climate model value. The Perseverance MEDA team reports a day-night difference of around 50 to 60 C (UPV/EHU release on Rodriguez-Manfredi et al. 2023).

precip.source: NASA Science, Mars Facts: the atmosphere is too thin for liquid water to last on the surface

ndvi.source: NASA Earth Observatory, Measuring Vegetation (NDVI and EVI): NDVI of 0.1 and below is barren rock, sand or snow
ndvi.note: Reference value for bare ground on Earth's NDVI scale. Not measured on Mars.

slope.source: MGS MOLA MEGDR 128 pixels per degree (NASA PDS), measured with pipeline/terrain_metrics.py over a 55.6 km window (validation/target_terrain.py)

roughness.source: MGS MOLA MEGDR 128 pixels per degree (NASA PDS), measured with pipeline/terrain_metrics.py over a 55.6 km window (validation/target_terrain.py)

lithology.source: Farley et al. 2022, Science 377:eabo2196 (crater floor is igneous: Maaz lava flows over the Seitah olivine-rich rock)
lithology.note: GLiM class 2, Basic volcanic rocks, for the lava flows the rover landed on. The delta to the west is sedimentary.

cannotCopy: Gravity: 3.73 m/s2 at the surface of Mars against 9.82 m/s2 on Earth, a little over one third (NASA NSSDC Mars Fact Sheet).
Thin atmosphere: the mean surface pressure is 6.36 mb (NASA NSSDC Mars Fact Sheet) against 1014 mb on Earth (NASA NSSDC Earth Fact Sheet), and it is mostly carbon dioxide.

Radiation: Curiosity's RAD instrument measured about 0.67 millisieverts per day on the surface from August 2012 to June 2013 (Southwest Research Institute release, 9 December 2013, on Hassler et al. 2014, Science).
No liquid water: the atmosphere is too thin for liquid water to last on the surface (NASA Science, Mars Facts), so Earth's rain, rivers and wet soil have no counterpart.

name: Gale crater
summary: A 154 km crater with a central mountain of layered sediments. NASA's Curiosity rover landed here in August 2012 and found deposits of an ancient lake that could have supported life (Grotzinger et al. 2014, Science).

tempMean.source: Mars Climate Database v6.2 (LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES), climatology scenario, air temperature 2 m above the surface (validation/build/mars_temperature.py)
tempMean.note: Climate model value, used so that all Mars targets share one definition. Curiosity's REMS record gives -43.7 C for the midpoint of the daily minimum and maximum, 11 C warmer than the model's figure for the same statistic. See data/REVIEW_ME.md.

tempRange.source: Curiosity REMS daily minimum and maximum air temperature, sols 10 to 4995, NASA Mars weather feed (Centro de Astrobiologia) (validation/build/mars_temperature.py)
tempRange.note: Mean daily maximum minus minimum of air temperature about 1.6 m above ground. The climate model gives 54 C.

name: Arcadia Planitia (site AP-1)
summary: Smooth northern plains with a layer of buried water ice tens of metres thick (Bramson et al. 2015, Geophysical Research Letters). Site AP-1 is one of four prime candidate landing sites studied for SpaceX Starship, chosen for its ice and safe terrain (Golombek et al. 2021, LPSC abstract 2420).
